PullRequest.Title: chat: Avoid transient sticky row rebuilds during resize
PullRequest.Body:

Part of #339863; this does not resolve the whole multi-pane resizing issue.

## Summary

Width layout clears the cached sticky source geometry, but previously deferred its measurement until the next animation frame. The existing tree refresh could therefore see estimated geometry, rebuild the sticky row, and then rebuild it again once the measured geometry arrived.

Run the existing source-range measurement synchronously before that tree refresh. This is one production method-call change: no generic-tree changes, new caching/lifetime machinery, debounce, setting, or skipped measurement. The existing width guard and content/source invalidation paths remain in place.

Add regression coverage for unchanged/height-only layout, width measurement and sticky/editor identity, focus/scroll anchors, and streaming/hidden updates using real code-block editors.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/tree/objectTree.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts` - **832 passing**, one pre-existing pending.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts --grep "width changes keep sticky templates and code editors while updating measured geometry"` - fails on the original baseline as expected; passes with this fix.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts` - passed.
- `git --no-pager diff --check` - passed.

Real current-source Code OSS Agents windows, inspected with `@hediet/dbgjs`, also passed streaming while user-scrolled, hidden updates, follow-tail, sticky transitions, sash dragging, font/zoom changes, code/diff model identity, drafts, focus, and removal/disposal checks.

## Native measurements

Compared base `564de3cb8366c7a23c2a1235ff3e8597566b4075`, an earlier broader optimization, and this smaller fix. Three fresh native lifecycles per variant in balanced order; 1/3/6 populated panes, eight Markdown/TypeScript-code-block turns per pane, and combined/height-only/width-only resizing: **81 scenarios**. Resizes use real `BrowserWindow.setBounds`. Complete lifecycles were serialized; scored timings use no profiler, trace, or operation-counting wrappers.

Six-pane medians:

| Metric | Base | Earlier broad patch | This one-call fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Combined: browser layouts / delivered resize | 131.32 | 119.43 | 119.34 |
| Combined: p95 frame gap | 84.2 ms | 66.7 ms | 66.8 ms |
| Width-only: browser layouts / delivered resize | 128.45 | 114.95 | 114.19 |
| Width-only: p95 frame gap | 67.0 ms | 43.5 ms | 43.2 ms |

The fixed combined p95 ranged from 66.7 to 66.9 ms across the three runs. Separate dbgjs counting found zero sticky row/template creations or disposals in the fixed six-pane combined resize run, versus about 1.29 per chat layout on the baseline.

These are local development-build observations, not statistical guarantees. Height-only work is essentially unchanged, and significant style/layout cost remains. No paid provider orchestration was involved. All temporary app/debugger processes and profiles were cleaned up.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each sticky-enabled width resize invalidated measured source geometry but deferred recomputation until after an immediate sticky-tree refresh, producing an estimated sticky state followed by a measured state and repeated sticky DOM/editor construction and disposal.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Width resizing a populated chat, especially across multiple panes, repeatedly rebuilt transient sticky rows and their heavyweight rendered content, increasing layout/render work and frame gaps.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed renderer.layout performs refreshStickyScrollSourceRanges synchronously after invalidating width-dependent ranges, so the immediate tree refresh consumes measured geometry and retains the existing sticky template instead of rendering an estimated row and rebuilding it after the animation-frame measurement.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: On a width change, ChatListWidget.layout calls tree.layout, then renderer.layout, then tree.refreshStickyScroll. In the base revision renderer.layout cleared stickyScrollSourceRangesByRequestId and only scheduled refreshStickyScrollSourceRanges for the next animation frame. The immediate tree refresh therefore received an estimated range from getStickyScrollSourceRange. StickyScrollWidget.setState renders a new state when measured height/source fields differ; the scheduled callback then measured request/sticky DOM bounds and refreshed the tree again, causing a second sticky-state render. The added test establishes that a real width change now measures geometry while preserving the same sticky row, bubble, and code-editor instances.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a populated chat pane horizontally while prompt-timeline sticky scroll is pinning a request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat host layout -> ChatWidget.layout -> ChatListWidget.layout -> tree.layout -> ChatListItemRenderer.layout -> synchronous source-range measurement -> updateBottomPadding -> tree.refreshStickyScroll. The changed DOM measurement is now on the resize critical path, but it supplies authoritative geometry before the tree refresh and avoids the prior estimated-state render followed by a measured-state rebuild.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Traverse currently rendered request and sticky templates and read request, row, parent, and sticky-row geometry with getBoundingClientRect, which may force browser style/layout resolution after tree and editor layout writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One traversal per distinct pane width; effective collection size is virtualized rendered request templates plus at most one sticky template because stickyScrollMaxItemCount is 1. In multi-pane resize this repeats once per resized visible pane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same geometry reads were scheduled and coalesced for the next animation frame. Before they ran, ChatListWidget.layout immediately refreshed sticky scroll against cleared ranges, producing estimated geometry; the deferred callback measured and refreshed again, potentially disposing and reconstructing the sticky row and its embedded editor content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff moves the existing measurement from the next animation frame onto resize completion before the immediate sticky-tree refresh. Although synchronous, this replaces an estimated sticky render and subsequent measured rebuild; repository call flow and the new identity regression test establish the eliminated repeated render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously visible chat panes times distinct delivered width changes, with per-pane geometry work bounded by virtualized rendered request templates rather than full transcript history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM/editor layout and sticky refresh work is serialized on the renderer/UI thread. Across multiple visible chat panes, each pane is laid out serially; within a pane, the width equality guard permits one changed-path execution per distinct delivered width.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Measured source ranges and request-width ratios are warm until width changes. The width guard skips unchanged and height-only layouts. A changed width invalidates both maps, then repopulates them synchronously; rejected/empty states remain represented in the range map. Existing animation-frame scheduling still coalesces height-driven refreshes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: layout ordering, cache invalidation, estimated fallback, DOM geometry reads, sticky-state equality, and renderState reconstruction are all explicit in the traced code; the added test verifies sticky DOM/editor identity across a real width change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact forced-layout duration and callback cadence vary with browser, pane count, and rendered request complexity. The code evidence establishes the removed double-render mechanism; no code evidence establishes that the moved synchronous read produces a net regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is a narrowly guarded performance fix: it moves an already-required measurement earlier to prevent transient sticky row/template reconstruction. The possible loss of scheduler coalescing does not establish a net user-visible degradation against the concretely removed rebuild, so no finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a chat pane vertically or repeat layout at the same width
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatListWidget.layout still performs tree layout, bottom-padding update, and sticky refresh, but ChatListItemRenderer.layout exits the changed width branch because newWidth equals the cached layout width. The changed source-range measurement is therefore off this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of height-only layout notifications during vertical sash dragging or host relayout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI thread; repeated height notifications may occur, but the production diff adds no work to them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Width-dependent source geometry remains warm because neither source-range nor width-ratio maps are cleared. Existing pending animation-frame refreshes retain their prior coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call is nested under the existing newWidth inequality guard, and the added test asserts zero sticky bubble bounds and row-height reads across repeated height-only layouts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for diff causality: the equality guard directly excludes this scenario from the changed operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; unchanged-width and height-only layouts do not execute the new synchronous measurement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream response content, update while hidden, and reveal the chat without changing pane width
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model progress -> widget refresh/render and item-height handling; request-source range refreshes remain driven by existing resize-observer/item-height scheduling. The changed renderer width branch is not reached unless reveal also changes width.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Streaming update frequency and number of virtualized visible rows; the diff does not increase either cardinality on a stable-width pane.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and DOM updates are serialized on the UI thread; existing source-range callbacks use one MutableDisposable per renderer to coalesce pending animation-frame work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Sticky request content and measured range caches remain valid at stable width. Hidden/revealed content does not clear width-dependent caches by itself; existing content/source invalidation remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole production change is inside width invalidation, while streaming and hidden updates use unchanged refresh/render paths; the added test covers sticky-template retention through those updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A simultaneous width change would enter the first resize scenario, but pure streaming/visibility updates do not reach the changed call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; stable-width streaming and visibility changes do not execute diff-introduced work, and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was added or moved.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. No actionable performance regression was found. The production change fixes repeated sticky-row reconstruction during width resize; the introducing base line was blamed and recorded as a regression fix. Test-only additions do not affect product runtime.
